decisions: Select Next.js App Router with strict TypeScript for the additive modernization shell.
Use a strangler migration with typed legacy adapters and one vertical slice at a time.
Keep the legacy application and persistence behavior authoritative until individual slices have characterization evidence and explicit approval.
risks: Next.js introduces Node runtime and deployment complexity.
Typed adapters can still encode legacy assumptions if a workflow is extracted without characterization evidence.
Routing rollback cannot undo incompatible future writes, so writing slices need separate data rollback plans.
dependencies: LAM-76 for the additive shell implementation.
LAM-77 for legacy characterization tests before workflow extraction or write enablement.
followUps: Implement the shell as an additive route or service with explicit feature gating.
Create a per-slice migration, compatibility, and data rollback plan before enabling writes.
Retire a legacy path only through a separately approved migration decision.
rollback: For the initial shell, disable its distinct route or feature flag and continue serving the unmodified legacy application. Do not couple the initial shell to destructive data changes. Any future slice that writes data must have an approved backward-compatible data rollback plan before rollout.
